Quick answers:
- EU Data Residency: Redwood supports contractually-enforceable EU-only processing for customer data in Hosted and Dedicated modes. Our customer data plane for eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 remains within EU physical regions; we can include an EU Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and add contractual flow-downs in the SOW.

- Private/VPC options:
  - VPC peering: Supported for Redwood Private customers. Peering uses private endpoints and strict security groups; no public egress is required.
  - On-prem package: For air-gapped or regulated environments, we provide an on-prem install with local KMS/HSM support.
  - Controls included: network ACLs, security groups, private endpoints, mTLS for internal service-to-service, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), per-request audit logging (retention configurable), and continuous monitoring hooks.

- Logging & Audit: Access logs and inference audit logs can be retained in-region; we can configure retention windows per contract. Audit logs are shipped to the customer's S3/GCS/Azure Blob in the same region for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- SIG/CAIQ & SOC2: The attached CAIQ maps to our SOC2 controls. SOC2 summary includes control narratives; full SOC2 report available under NDA.

Hi Daniel — short technical note to supplement Neha's attachments.

VPC peering / Private deployment details (summary):
- Peering model: Customer creates VPC in their cloud account; Redwood sets up a peering connection to our Private control plane endpoints in the same region. All traffic uses private IP ranges (RFC1918).
- Endpoints: We publish per-tenant private endpoints; customers can restrict ingress to specific subnets.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported via BYOK. Keys remain in customer's KMS and are used for encrypting persisted artifacts.
- Audit logs: Delivered to customer bucket with server-side encryption; log events include request-id, model_id, user_id (pseudonymized on request), and region.
- Failover: For Dedicated customers we support regional failover to a pre-agreed compatible region within EU (e.g., eu-central -> eu-west) under SLA; cross-border failover requires explicit contractual approval.
- Minimal ACL example (for procurement): allow TCP 443 from Redwood peering CIDR to the private endpoints, deny all others; route tables should be explicit for the peering connection.

If Eversafe needs a short statement for legal: "Redwood will ensure all customer inference data for the contracted tenant is stored and processed solely within the EU regions specified in the SOW; no replication to the US occurs without prior written consent." We can sign and return that as redwood-eu-hosting-statement.txt attached.

Happy to run a short session with your infra/security architects to walk through the diagram and recommended ACLs.

—Vivek Kulkarni
